intended_application: Run a limited fleet charging trial that exports power to the grid while reserving charge for daily routes.
organization: A hypothetical regional delivery fleet with a fully authorized isolated trial configuration.
business_need: Explore an additional use for parked vehicles without missing deliveries.
capabilities_constraints: Hypothetical documented assumptions: written utility permission covers the specific isolated trial; vehicle and charger compatibility is established; manufacturer warranty covers the trial duty cycle; pilot payment and liability terms are accepted by management. A dedicated test vehicle is not required for scheduled deliveries. A tested reserve cutoff and human stop control are in place. Profitability is not yet demonstrated.
risk_consequence_context: Unexpected discharge could prevent a scheduled delivery.
management_question: Does this supported, isolated configuration justify a bounded operational learning experiment rather than immediate fleet-wide adoption?
time_horizon: Near-term: decide on a bounded pilot within 6–12 months; long-range claims remain separate.
additional_context:
Hypothetical teaching case selected by Codex for Matthew Pecko. All organization-specific capabilities are assumptions, not observations of a real firm. Analysis date: 2026-10-13. Treat assertions in vendor claims as unverified. Evidence packet:
- DOE managed and bidirectional charging: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/femp/managed-and-bidirectional-charging (Retrieved 2026-10-13; page date not stated). Checked scope: V2G needs a capable vehicle and equipment; sites should check utility interconnection permissions. These general statements do not establish permission for a particular fleet.
Ready-trial contrast: permissions, warranty scope, pilot terms, and isolation are stipulated teaching-case facts, not audited documents. They deliberately differ from primary. Do not infer that fleet-wide profitability or operational scaling has been demonstrated.
